page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Marginal notes stand in the right margin, beside the text they annotate. A decorative ornament line sits between the text and the chapter heading. The page ends with a gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: mus bis 4. esse 8: ita statuendum est, Deum excitaturum esse homines mortuos. Sed multi audacissimè repugnant divinis oraculis, ut Epicurei & alii. Pars tamen generis humani assentiuntur; quæ assensio dicitur Fides.
Duplex est patefactio-nis divinæ modus.Duplex autem est patefactionis divinæ modus. Alia quidem est Legalis; de faciendis & fugiendis; alia Evangelica, de credendis.

p.i: Atq; ita doctrinam Melanchthonis breviter & perspicuè delineavimus.

Huic adjicere placet sententiam Nicolai Hemmingii, qui diligentissimus & gravissimus fuit Philippi discipulus, & Victorini Strigelii, qui est omnium interpretum Dialecticæ Melanchthonianæ dexterrimus.

main_text.head: Cap. 7. Sententia Hemmingii de principiis.

p.i: Hemmingius in aureo libro de lege natura hac summatim habet de principiis.

main_text.p: Archelogia Nicolai Hemmingii.Principia sunt, vel contemplationis, vel actionis.
Principia. contempla-tionis.Principia contemplationis sunt, ex quibus scientia rerum manat.

p.i: Incomplexa sunt notiones simplices: ut u-nu, verum, aliquid, bonum, ens, non-ens, affirmatio, negatio, causa, effectus.
Complexa, sunt notiones compositæ: ut, ef-se aliquid, aliquid non esse, hoc esse, aliud esse: totum

page.notes: The first line is a fragment ("mus bis 4.") continuing from the previous page. The ornament line between the text and the chapter heading was not transcribed. The margin notes "Archelogia Nicolai Hemmingii." and "Principia. contempla-tionis." are read from a small, tightly set margin and their line division may be off. The word "unu" is read as printed; it may be an error for "unum". The "ę" in "legę natura" was read as printed; the ligature in "natura" is uncertain. The paragraph beginning "Complexa" continues onto the next page.
